Day 1 of 9: June 15, 2024, Santorini, Greece

June 15, 2024

Santorini, Greece

Arrived in Santorini and witnessed the legendary sunset at Oia. The caldera turned deep blue as the sun melted into the Aegean.

June 16, 2024

Athens, Greece

Early morning at the Acropolis to beat the crowds. The Parthenon is humbling — 2,500 years old and still standing.

June 17, 2024

Delphi, Greece

Drove to ancient Delphi, home of the Oracle. The mountain sanctuary feels mystical even today.

June 18, 2024

Meteora, Greece

Monasteries perched on impossible rock pillars. Monks built these 600 years ago without modern tools — humbling.

June 19, 2024

Thessaloniki, Greece

Second city, first impressions. Byzantine walls, Ottoman markets, and the best street food in Greece.

June 20, 2024

Olympus Base, Greece

Attempted the trail to Mount Olympus. Made it halfway before weather turned. Zeus had other plans.

June 21, 2024

Halkidiki Peninsula, Greece

Three-fingered peninsula. Turquoise water, pine forests to the beach, and finally some quiet.

June 22, 2024

Crete, Greece

Flew to Crete, largest of the Greek islands. Starting in Heraklion, heading to Knossos tomorrow.

June 23, 2024

Knossos, Crete

Palace of Minos. 4,000 years old. The reconstruction is controversial but gives you a sense of the scale.

June 15, 2024

Santorini, Greece

Sunny, 28°C150 miles

Sunset at Oia

Arrived in Santorini this morning. The famous blue-domed churches are even more stunning in person. Spent the afternoon exploring the narrow streets of Oia, getting lost in the maze of white-washed buildings.

Evening brought the legendary sunset. Hundreds of tourists gathered, but somehow it felt intimate. The sun melted into the Aegean, painting everything gold and orange. The caldera below turned deep blue.

Had dinner at a taverna overlooking the sea. Fresh octopus, Greek salad, and local wine. The owner told stories about the island before tourism took over.
